name: Octaves
description: Adds the notes you play one and two octaves down and up, chords included, with no audible delay and no warble.

params.name: Two down
params.description: The level of the voice two octaves below what you play. It gives the weight of organ pedals; notes below about the A at 110 Hz are left out of it because they would land under hearing.

params.name: One down
params.description: The level of the voice one octave below what you play. It follows chords note for note, like a bass player doubling every string.

params.name: Dry
params.description: The level of your own sound, passed through untouched and in stereo. Turn it down to hear only the octaves.

params.name: One up
params.description: The level of the voice one octave above what you play. It adds the shimmer of a second, higher set of strings.

params.name: Two up
params.description: The level of the voice two octaves above what you play. Thin and bright, like the top stop of an organ.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How long the octaves take to fade in after each new note. At zero they start with the note; longer times let the pick or hammer through alone and bring the octaves in behind it like a bowed pad.

params.name: Filter
params.description: A low-pass on the octave voices only. Turn it down to round off the upper octaves or to leave the low ones as a soft bass.

params.name: Resonance
params.description: A peak at the filter frequency, on the octave voices only. A little gives them a vocal, nasal edge; a lot makes the filter ring.

params.name: Detune
params.description: Pulls each octave voice slightly out of tune, each its own way, by up to 15 cents. It makes the slow beating of a twelve-string or of a rank of organ pipes that are not quite in tune.

params.name: Spread
params.description: Places the notes of the two upper voices at different points between left and right. The lower octaves stay in the middle, and the sound sums to mono without loss.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. The method is filter-bank phase scaling after Etienne Thuillier, 'Real-Time Polyphonic Octave Doubling for the Guitar' (Aalto University MSc thesis, 2016), as also used in Steve Schulteis's open poly octave work: narrow complex band-pass channels, each played back with its phase doubled or halved. The channel shape, the phase equaliser, the channels that widen for a moment at each new note, and the sub-octave phase tracking are this device's own.
